forces.title: Easing recruitment difficulties across Norwegian economy.
forces.description: Multiple Norges Bank reports indicate a sustained easing of recruitment difficulties across Norway, with a lower share of contacts reporting skilled labour shortages compared to historical averages. This trend may reduce the urgency and volume of demand for external staffing services as clients find it easier to recruit directly or face less competition for talent.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: AI deployment dampens labour demand for entry-level roles.
forces.description: The increased use of Artificial Intelligence is dampening overall labour demand in Norway, particularly impacting large firms and entry-level positions. This structural shift implies that routine tasks are becoming increasingly automated, reducing the need for human personnel in these segments. Staffing firms face a challenge in adapting their offerings away from traditional entry-level placements.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 1/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Clients internalising tasks reduces demand for contract personnel.
forces.description: A growing trend in Norway sees customers opting to perform an increasing share of tasks themselves rather than relying on external contract personnel or consultancy services. This direct internalisation of work reduces the addressable market for staffing firms, particularly those providing temporary or project-based placements, forcing them to demonstrate clear value beyond basic labour supply.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 1/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Automation and insourcing reduce external labour demand in Food & Beverage.
forces.description: Irish food and beverage producers are increasingly investing in automation, robotics, and integrated production methods to offset labour shortages and manage costs. Furthermore, businesses are bringing selected outsourced activities in-house. These strategies directly reduce the demand for external staffing services, including HR outsourcing and contract labour, presenting a significant headwind for human capital providers in this sector.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Hospitality sector adopts technology to reduce workforce and automate tasks.
forces.description: The Irish hospitality sector is implementing technology, including AI and automation, for rostering, back-office processes, and guest communications. This shift is part of a strategy to reduce operational friction and reframe labour strategy around a smaller, more skilled workforce, thereby lowering demand for traditional staffing roles and impacting firms supplying general or lower-skilled personnel to the industry.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Job reductions in tech sector attributed to AI deployment.
forces.description: Despite Ireland's strong position as a technology hub, job reductions in global tech companies are being attributed to AI deployment, leading to a drop in graduate hiring as routine tasks like payroll and credit control are automated. This trend signals a shift in talent demand away from generalist or administrative roles, posing a challenge for staffing firms that focus on supplying these profiles to the tech sector.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

forces.title: Increased insolvencies in client sectors dampens demand for staffing.
forces.description: Increased insolvencies in the Irish retail and hospitality sectors pose a sensitive risk to staffing firms. As these client industries face structural weaknesses and an unfavourable outlook, business failures directly translate into reduced demand for temporary, contract, and permanent placements. Staffing providers need to diversify client portfolios and be agile in anticipating sector-specific downturns.
forces.source_title: 2025 Ireland economic outlook: Resilience amid global uncertainty

forces.title: Persistent workforce availability challenges in healthcare sector.
forces.description: The Irish healthcare sector continues to grapple with significant workforce availability challenges, driving sustained demand for staffing solutions across nursing homes, disability services, and homecare. Despite efforts to integrate technology, the fundamental need for human resources to manage complex care needs and an aging population ensures continued opportunities for staffing and human capital firms specializing in this sector.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Shift in recruitment to AI-related capabilities and internal upskilling.
forces.description: Irish organizations are modifying recruitment strategies to prioritize AI-related capabilities, with 60% of respondents making changes to their graduate recruitment. The emergence of 'vibe coding' suggests a future where external hiring needs could be reduced as companies retrain and upskill existing employees to become 'citizen developers,' fundamentally altering the demand landscape for traditional external recruitment.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Strong demand for staffing in defense, health, and energy sectors.
forces.description: Norwegian recruitment agencies are experiencing a rise in demand for staffing services from specific growth sectors, including defense, emergency preparedness, health, aquaculture, and energy. This sector-specific tailwind offsets broader market softening in areas like construction, indicating opportunities for staffing firms with specialized expertise and client focus within these robust industries.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 4/2025: Somewhat lower capacity utilisation

forces.title: Rising labour costs squeeze client margins, impacting staffing demand.
forces.description: Irish businesses across various sectors (food & beverage, hospitality, retail) face rising labour costs due to minimum wage increases, pension auto-enrolment, and PRSI contributions. This intensifies pressure on client margins, leading them to focus on cost discipline and operational efficiency. This may translate into reduced demand for external staffing or increased pressure on staffing firms to offer more cost-effective or flexible solutions.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Hospitality Sector H2 2025 Insights and H1 2026 Outlook

forces.title: New regulatory staffing mix and permit thresholds increase costs.
forces.description: The Irish healthcare sector faces increased cost pressures from regulatory changes, including minimum annual remuneration thresholds for employment permits and the operational impact of the 50:50 staffing mix requirement. These policies particularly affect providers reliant on international recruitment, impacting the cost structure and service delivery models of staffing firms specializing in sourcing talent from abroad for the healthcare industry.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Low construction activity dampens recruitment agency order volumes.
forces.description: Low construction activity in Norway is directly dampening order volumes for recruitment agencies. As the construction sector experiences weak new-builds and postponed projects, its demand for labour, including temporary and contract staff, declines. This creates a specific headwind for staffing firms with significant exposure to the construction industry, necessitating diversification or a focus on other growth sectors.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 4/2025: Somewhat lower capacity utilisation

forces.title: Skills shortages drive demand for specialized talent acquisition.
forces.description: Despite overall employment stability, the Irish manufacturing sector continues to face labour shortages in specific skill sets, acting as a key constraint on growth potential. These persistent skills gaps create an ongoing demand for staffing firms that can effectively source and place specialized talent, highlighting opportunities for providers focusing on niche areas and high-demand professional roles.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Manufacturing Sector H2 2025 Insights and H1 2026 Outlook

forces.title: Client recruitment and retention challenges bolster staffing demand.
forces.description: Recruitment and retention of personnel remain key challenges for clients in the Irish retail and hospitality sectors, despite some improvements. This ongoing difficulty for businesses to attract and keep staff in a competitive environment creates a sustained demand for external staffing and human capital services, as clients seek support to fill vacancies and manage their workforce needs effectively.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Retail Sector H2 2025 Insights and H1 2026 Outlook

viewpoints.title: Norwegian labour market tightness eases, but skilled staff recruitment remains challenging.
viewpoints.description: Norges Bank contacts observe a decrease in overall recruitment difficulties and a lower share of firms reporting full capacity utilisation. This suggests an easing in the general labour market, potentially reducing immediate demand for external staffing solutions. However, challenges persist in finding experienced and qualified personnel across various sectors, indicating ongoing demand for specialized recruitment services despite broader softening.
viewpoints.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

viewpoints.title: Hospitality sector to reframe labour strategy towards smaller, skilled teams.
viewpoints.description: The Irish hospitality sector is urged to reframe its labour strategy, focusing on a smaller, more skilled workforce and leveraging technology to automate repetitive tasks. This shift aims to redeploy staff to high-value guest-facing services, indicating a structural change that could reduce overall demand for traditional staffing, especially for entry-level or routine roles, while increasing demand for training and upskilling services.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: AI adoption and automation driving targeted job reductions in tech and routine tasks.
viewpoints.description: Job losses in the Irish tech sector are increasingly attributed to AI deployment, especially for automating routine tasks like payroll and credit control. This trend suggests a structural shift where technology reduces demand for entry-level and administrative roles, posing a challenge for staffing firms focused on these segments. The emphasis is shifting towards rebalancing roles and evolving skills needs rather than pure job creation.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

viewpoints.title: Increased insolvencies in client sectors pose sensitive risks for staffing firms.
viewpoints.description: Rising insolvencies in the retail and hospitality sectors in Ireland, which are key clients for staffing firms, are identified as a sensitive risk. This indicates structural weaknesses and an unfavourable outlook for client demand, as business failures directly translate to reduced need for temporary, contract, or permanent placements from staffing providers. Smaller firms in these client sectors are particularly vulnerable.
viewpoints.source_title: 2025 Ireland economic outlook: Resilience amid global uncertainty

viewpoints.title: Workforce shortages in healthcare persist, but automation may temper staffing demand.
viewpoints.description: Ireland's healthcare sector continues to face significant challenges with workforce availability, which drives persistent demand for staffing solutions across residential care, disability services, and homecare. However, the sector is also investing in AI and automation for administrative efficiency, rostering, and documentation, indicating a potential moderation in demand for certain human roles as technology integration advances.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: AI expected to dampen labour demand in Norway, particularly for entry-level roles.
viewpoints.description: Norges Bank contacts anticipate that AI will have a dampening effect on overall labour demand in Norway in 2026, a significant shift from its neutral impact in 2025. This effect is expected to be most pronounced among large firms and for entry-level employees, suggesting a structural headwind for staffing firms providing general or less skilled labour, requiring a focus on higher-skilled or specialized placements.
viewpoints.source_title: Regional Network report 1/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

viewpoints.title: Recruitment difficulties increase across Norway, indicating stronger demand for staffing.
viewpoints.description: Norges Bank's Regional Network contacts report an uptick in recruitment difficulties, with 25% citing it as a primary constraint on output, the highest share in two years. This suggests a tightening labour market and increased demand for external staffing services as companies struggle to find the necessary personnel to meet their operational needs, creating a tailwind for recruitment agencies.
viewpoints.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2025: Stable growth prospects

pnl_drivers.description: Expected annual wage growth of 4.5% in 2026 and 4.0% in 2027 in Norway (Norges Bank report from 2026-09-17). Also, 4.5% for 2026 and 4.1% for 2027 (Norges Bank report from 2026-06-11). And 4.2% for 2026 and 3.9% for 2027 (Norges Bank report from 2026-03-19). This increases the cost base for staffing firms, which typically pass these costs through to clients with a markup, impacting revenue and potentially margin if not managed effectively against client price sensitivity.

market_sizing.methodology: Average expected annual wage growth rates among Norges Bank's Regional Network contacts.
market_sizing.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

pnl_drivers.description: Irish healthcare providers face material increases in staffing costs, including minimum wage hikes of approximately 6% in 2025 and 4.8% in 2026, plus broader inflation of over 2.5%. Additional pressures arise from increased minimum annual remuneration thresholds for employment permits and the operational impact of the 50:50 staffing mix requirement, especially for providers reliant on international recruitment. These costs significantly increase the expense base for staffing firms serving this sector.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of operating cost components and statutory increases affecting staffing expenses for client sectors in Ireland.
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026
